`--enable-http2` runs the ASGI app under Granian, which advertises Granian's
built-in `SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS` value. That value is not

## Purpose — why this change exists

The Triton W4A16 dense GEMM's tile table routes gfx90a into its **MI300
branch, tuned for 304 CUs**. An MI210 has 104. At decode widths that starves

title: [ROCm] fix sleep mode not releasing GPU memory problem on ROCm
body:
## Purpose
On ROCm, `hipMemRelease` does not return physical VRAM to the free pool
while the virtual-address reservation (from `hipMemAddressReserve`) is still
held. This causes sleep mode to report memory as freed at the HIP runtime
level, but the GPU VRAM remains occupied at the hardware level (confirmed via
`rocm-smi`), preventing other applications (e.g. RL training frameworks) from
using the freed memory.

at the end of `unmap_and_release` on the ROCm path. This forces the driver to
actually release the physical pages while immediately re-reserving the same

On the NPU GDN (gated delta net) **prefill** path, every GDN layer's chunked
delta-rule call recomputes the *same* chunk metadata — chunk indices/offsets for
`cumsum`, `chunk64`, and the `solve_tril` large-block — and issues per-layer
scalar device-to-host (D2H) syncs to read sequence lengths. For Qwen3.5-class
models the GDN layers dominate (e.g. 48 of 64 layers), so these per-layer
recomputations and D2H stalls accumulate and inflate prefill latency / TTFT.

This PR builds that metadata **once per prefill step** and reuses it across all
GDN layers, and passes a host-side `cu_seqlens_cpu` so the kernel reads the
sequence length without a D2H sync.

NPU-only; FLA chunk logic only. **Depends on the sgl-kernel-npu chunk changes in
sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu#454 — that kernel PR must be merged first.** Refs #24597.

title: [MoE] Add FlashInfer SM120 W4A8 MegaMoE backend for DeepSeek-V4-Flash
body:
## Summary This PR adds an opt-in `flashinfer_megamoe` runner backend for DeepSeek-V4-Flash with MXFP4 expert weights and MXFP8 activations on SM120 GPUs. The backend calls FlashInfer's public `flashinfer.moe_ep` interface and replaces the routed MoE sequence `dispatch -> FC1 -> FC2 -> combine` with a FlashInfer `MoEEpLayer`. The initial supported configuration is: ```bash --tp-size 4 \ --dp-size 4 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --ep-size 4 \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe \ --flashinfer-megamoe-max-num-tokens 8192 ```

With DP attention enabled, each rank owns a different DP token stream when entering the MoE layers. The adapter communicates the maximum active token count across ranks to FlashInfer and supports ranks with zero local tokens.

Existing MoE backends are unchanged unless flashinfer_megamoe is selected explicitly. …[truncated]

title: [Kernel] Optimize moeTopK memory access with shared memory and fix indexing bugs
body:
## Purpose
This PR improves the performance and correctness of the `moeTopK` kernel.

1. **Performance Optimization:** Optimized `indices` access by caching prior winning experts in Shared Memory. This reduces redundant Global Memory reads, which is highly effective when `k` is large.
2. **Bugfix (Logic)**: Fixed a potential bug where the `start_expert` offset was not applied consistently during index comparisons. title: [Perf] Route long standard-dispatch deep_gemm prefill through the contiguous grouped GEMM
body:
Long eager prefills on the deep_gemm MoE runner currently go through the masked grouped GEMM, a capacity-style interface built for CUDA-graph decode: it allocates [E, m_max, ...] buffers and launches far more kernels than the contiguous grouped GEMM the DeepEP paths already use. This adds a standard-dispatch contiguous pre-permute (ep_scatter + m_indices, per-expert counts from a GPU histogram so there is no per-layer device sync) and routes prefills above a token floor to it.

Scope: only the (standard dispatch, deep_gemm) pre-permute, and only for fp8 activations at block_shape [128, 128] -- the sole recipe this pre-permute can produce. bf16 weights (block_shape unset) and mxfp8 (block_shape [1, 32]) keep the masked path.
